openIssues.title: #24 wrong-account copy needs the owner login, which the #59 API does not expose when not connected
openIssues.body:
Found by QA while checking PR #81 (#59) against the approved #24 design (`docs/design/features/24-settings-projects.html`, version `8d65b7c`).

**What:** the approved wrong-account copy `gh.error.account` needs two logins: "GitHub was signed in as `{who}`. The console connects only to the owner's account, `{login}` …". #59's callback redirect gives only `{who}` (`/settings?github=wrong-account&login=<who>`). `GET /api/v1/github/connection` returns the owner's `login` only while connected, so on a first connect the client has nowhere to get `{login}` from. Client constants are not allowed for this (PR #42 security note 3).

Also, the callback's generic `github=failed` outcome (code refused, exchange or `/user` failure, non-expiring tokens, cookie or state refusals) has no copy in the approved design. Only `url`, `denied` and `account` do.

**Expected:** either the API exposes the configured owner login (for example `GET /connection` → `{ state: 'not-connected', ownerLogin }`, or `&owner=` on the wrong-account redirect), or #24's copy drops `{login}` for the not-connected case. A "failed" copy is added to #24's strings.
**Severity:** Low (copy/contract detail; #24 has not been built yet).

openIssues.title: Owner connection hardening follow-ups from PR #81 (reconnect chain, grant revoke scope, disconnect outcome, no-store)
openIssues.body:
Follow-ups from the security review of PR #81 (#59). None of these is exploitable for token theft today; they are the listed risks plus small gaps.

1. **Reconnect leaves the previous refresh chain live** (`apps/api/src/owner/owner-connection.ts:141-156`). A reconnect while connected overwrites the row without revoking the old pair. The old refresh token can still be rotated by anyone who copied it, until it expires (months) or the owner runs "Revoke all user tokens". Fix: before `repo.connect`, open the previous access token and call `DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token`. Log and continue on failure, and add a test. Check first whether GitHub revokes the paired refresh token with it. If not, document that reconnect is not a remediation and point the runbook at "Revoke all user tokens".
2. **A failure after the exchange on a reconnect revokes the whole grant** (`apps/api/src/routes/github-connection.ts:205-216`). `revokeUnwanted` calls `DELETE …/grant`. When the owner reconnects and `/user` or D1 fails, this also kills the stored connection's tokens. It fails safe (the next refresh drops the row with a security signal), but it is a surprising disconnect. Fix: revoke only the fresh token (`DELETE …/token`) when the login is already the owner's or is unknown. Keep grant revocation for a stranger's login.
3. **`DELETE /connection` after a decrypt failure or rotated key answers 204 while the grant is still live** (`owner-connection.ts:162-175`). #24 cannot tell this from a cle

openIssues.title: Registry: archived repos can never be re-added (stale installation_id has no recovery); 1-char repo names need a slug the UI cannot send
openIssues.body:
**QA finding** (from the PR #80 review, #15)

Two edge cases in the registry's add path that need a decision. Neither is covered by #15's acceptance criteria.

1. **An archived repo can never be added again, and neither can its slug.** `ProjectsRepo.findConflict` and the `INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS` count archived rows (`libs/worker/db/src/lib/projects.repo.ts`). Restore is out of scope, so the owner has no way back from an archive through the console. This also blocks the recovery that migration 0006's comment and the PR describe for rows with no or a stale `installation_id` ("until they are added again"): re-adding answers 409 `project-exists`. #12 would ignore that project's events.
   - Repro: add `geeera/private-product`, archive it, then add it again → 409 `project-exists` "An archived project already uses this slug or repository (private-product)".
   - Suggest one of: refresh `installation_id` during the setup check, or make restore/re-add the #24 open question 2 follow-up.
2. **Repositories with a one-character name cannot be added without an explicit `slug`.** `slugFromRepoName("x")` → `x`, which fails `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,38}$`, so the answer is 422 `validation`, step `slug`. The #24 design has only a slug *preview*, not a slug field, so the owner cannot fix this from the UI. The same happens for names that are only punctuation (`geeera/___`).
   - Repro: `POST /api/v1/projects {"repo":"geeera/x"}` → 422 step `slug`.

openIssues.title: Setup status lacks what the approved #24 design needs: last event time, server install URL, per-step unknowns
openIssues.body:
**QA finding** (from the PR #80 review, #15)

The setup status `GET /api/v1/projects/:slug/setup` matches #15's acceptance criteria exactly, but the approved #24 design (PR #42, `8d65b7c`, `docs/design/features/24-settings-projects.html`) needs three more things from it. Without them the setup page can only show part of the approved design.

1. **Step 4 "Events arrive", Done state.** The design's copy is `step.events.done`: "Last event at {time}." / «Последнее событие в {time}.». The DTO only has `events: 'seen' | 'never'`, so there is no time to show. Needs `lastEventAt: string | null` from #12's `webhook_deliveries`. The developer noted this on #15 too. `never` → «Ждём»/Waiting works as it is.
2. **Step 1 missing on the setup page** (for example, the app was uninstalled after the project was added). #24's AC says "missing: a link to the install page from the server". `installUrl` is only in the add refusal (409 `github-app-not-installed`); the setup DTO has none, so the client would have to build the URL itself, which the AC rules out.

openIssues.title: API JSON responses lack Cache-Control: no-store (private repo metadata cacheable)
openIssues.body:
**QA finding** (from the QA review of PR #74, #9)

Successful JSON responses of the `api` Worker carry no `Cache-Control` header, while every Problem Details response has `Cache-Control: no-store` (`libs/worker/core/src/lib/problem.ts:30`). With #9, `GET /api/v1/projects/:slug/repository` returns data about private repositories (`"private": true`, default branch). Without `no-store` or `private`, a browser or an intermediate cache may keep it after the session ends. The pre-existing `GET /api/v1/projects` behaves the same, so this is API-wide and was not introduced by #74.

**Steps to reproduce** (commit 142f10e, local mock mode):
1. `wrangler dev --config apps/api/wrangler.jsonc --env dev --var ENVIRONMENT:local --var AUTH_MODE:local --var GITHUB_MOCK:true`, with a project row for `geeera/private-product`.
2. `curl -sD - http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/v1/projects/<slug>/repository`

**Expected:** `Cache-Control: no-store` (or `private, no-store`) on authenticated API JSON, like the error responses.
**Actual:** `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/json`, no `Cache-Control`.

Suggested fix: a default `Cache-Control: no-store` for `/api/*` in `createWorkerApp`, plus one test. For `security` to confirm the severity.

openIssues.title: workspace-checks may not run on dev PRs that only change a wrangler.jsonc (no Nx dependency on api/hooks)
openIssues.body:
Found during the security review of PR #70 (outside that PR's scope).

**What:** `tools/workspace-checks/src/worker-config.spec.ts` is the only check that parses `apps/api/wrangler.jsonc` and `apps/hooks/wrangler.jsonc` with wrangler's own reader (`unstable_readConfig`) and asserts each env has exactly one `DB` D1 binding and that api/hooks share the same `database_id`. It reads those files at runtime by path, but `tools/workspace-checks/project.json` declares no `implicitDependencies` on `api`/`hooks` (and no `namedInputs` covering `apps/*/wrangler.jsonc`).

**Why it matters (suspected, not reproduced — Nx not run):** on a PR into `dev` that only touches a `wrangler.jsonc`, `ci.yml` picks `nx affected` (the file is not in its `root_config` list), so `workspace-checks` is likely not affected and does not run. A PR could then drop an env's `d1_databases`, or drift api's `database_id` from hooks', and merge into `dev` green; the deploy guard (`tools/deploy-guard/check-d1-placeholder.js`) only rejects the exact placeholder id. Release PRs into stage/main use `run-many`, so the gap is limited to `dev`. Impact: a broken or split-database dev deploy (integrity/availability), no data exposure.

**Fix:** add `"implicitDependencies": ["api", "hooks"]` to `tools/workspace-checks/project.json` (or an input on `{workspaceRoot}/apps/*/wrangler.jsonc`), then confirm with `npx nx show projects --affected --files=apps/api/wrangler.jsonc` that `workspace-checks` is listed.

openIssues.body:
Found in the round-2 security review of PR #57 (ADR 0003). This risk predates that PR: #10's architect note accepted it for the repo-only PAT. ADR 0003 makes it concrete, because it asks the owner to press **Connect GitHub in stage** so the Playwright e2e (#14) can answer through the Access service identity.

**Why it matters.** The dev and stage "sandbox product" is `geeera/team-console`, and that is not a throwaway repo. - the Access service token (`CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` in the `stage` GitHub Environment)

openIssues.title: JWKS: negative-cache failed key-set loads
openIssues.body:
From the PR #55 security review (non-blocking): `apps/api/src/auth/access-jwt.ts` does not remember a failed JWKS load. While the certs endpoint is down, or ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN is valid-looking but wrong, every well-formed token triggers a new fetch (probe: 10 requests → 10 fetches). Still fails closed.

Fix: negative-cache a failed load per URL for a few seconds; add a spec. Also assert `redirect: manual` on the JWKS fetch so a jose upgrade can't silently change it.

openIssues.title: /api and /api/ are answered by the SPA fallback instead of a problem+json 404
openIssues.body:
Found by QA while reviewing PR #49 (#6), head 7e86d41.

**Steps** (Docker image from #49, or `npx nx serve api`)
- `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/api` → `200 text/html` (the app shell, no `X-Request-Id`)
- `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/` → `200 text/html`
- `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/API/v1/healthz` → `200 text/html`
- whereas `/api/v1`, `/api/v1/`, `/api/v1/nope`, `/api/v2/x` → `404 application/problem+json` (correct)

**Expected** (architect note on #6, decision 19): paths under `/api` are never answered by the SPA fallback; a client that calls `/api` or `/api/` gets a Problem Details 404.

**Actual**: `run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]` does not route `/api` and `/api/` to the Worker, so the assets layer's `single-page-application` fallback answers them with `index.html`.

**Suggested direction**: `run_worker_first: ["/api", "/api/*"]` (check what wrangler 4.124 matches for `/api/`), plus an app.spec case for `/api` and `/api/`.

Severity low: #6's criterion covers `/api/v1/*`, which behaves correctly; no real client calls these bare paths.

openIssues.title: Local nx serve hooks uses its own unmigrated D1, not the api Worker's
openIssues.body:
Found by QA while reviewing PR #49 (#6), head 7e86d41.

**Where**: `apps/hooks/wrangler.jsonc`, `apps/hooks/project.json` (`serve` target), `CLAUDE.md` "Workers (#6)".

**Steps**
1. Fresh clone, `npm ci`.
2. `npx nx serve api` (runs `api:migrate`), then `npx nx serve hooks` (depends on `api:migrate`, listens on :8788).
3. Inspect local D1 state: `apps/api/.wrangler/state/v3/d1/...sqlite` has `d1_migrations, projects`; `apps/hooks/.wrangler/state/v3/d1/` holds no database with those tables.

**Expected**: locally, as in the deployed environments, the hooks Worker reads the same migrated `team-console-dev` database as the api Worker (the `serve` dependency on `api:migrate` implies this).

**Actual**: wrangler keeps local state next to each config (`apps/<app>/.wrangler`), so `nx serve hooks` runs against a separate, never-migrated local D1. Anything #12 adds that touches `DB` from the hooks Worker locally will fail with `no such table`.

**Suggested direction**: a shared `--persist-to` (e.g. `.wrangler/state` at the workspace root) for `api:migrate`, `api:serve` and `hooks:serve`, or run both Workers in one `wrangler dev -c apps/api/wrangler.jsonc -c apps/hooks/wrangler.jsonc` session.

Not blocking #6: its acceptance criteria concern the api Worker and the hooks `/healthz`, which does not use D1. Unit tests are unaffected (they migrate an in-memory D1 per file).

openIssues.title: Scanner pins in security.yml (gitleaks, semgrep image) are outside Dependabot's reach
openIssues.body:
Found by the security review of PR #47 (Dependabot for github-actions).

`.github/dependabot.yml` only watches `uses:` references. `.github/workflows/security.yml` also pins two scanner versions in `env:`, and Dependabot never looks at those:
- `GITLEAKS_VERSION: 8.30.1` + `GITLEAKS_SHA256` (release binary, checksum-verified)
- `SEMGREP_IMAGE: semgrep/semgrep:1.177.0@sha256:…`

The pins are safe: they are exact and verified. The risk is that they go stale. Scanner rule and detector updates, plus fixes in the tools themselves, never arrive unless someone bumps them by hand. So the secret-scan and SAST gates slowly lose coverage without any sign that this is happening.

Fix (pick one):
1. Add a scheduled reminder, e.g. a monthly check in the deep audit that compares the pins with the latest upstream releases, and bump them in a reviewed PR that updates the checksum.
2. Or move Semgrep to a `container:`/`docker://` form that Dependabot's `docker` ecosystem can track, and keep gitleaks on the manual bump with the checksum.

Severity low: nothing is exploitable today; this is about detection quality over time.

openIssues.title: Notification privacy: hide details on the lock screen, manage devices
openIssues.body:
From the security threat model on #11 (row 9) and row 8: notifications show issue titles from private repositories on a locked phone, and a lost or retired device keeps receiving them until it is removed.

**User story.** As the owner, I want to hide notification details on the lock screen and remove old devices, so that private project titles do not show on a phone someone else can see.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Settings has a "Hide details on the lock screen" switch; when it is on, pushes carry a generic body ("New item in {project}") and the title is shown only inside the app
- [ ] Settings lists the devices subscribed to push (device type, added, last delivered), and each can be removed
- [ ] The choice is stored on the server and applies to every device
- [ ] All strings via i18n (ru, en); axe clean

## Out of scope
- Per-project notification rules
- Quiet hours

`team:pm-chat` issue per product, full history, posting messages, waking the product's PM routine through the hooks
Worker (retry queue, Retry-After), reply push. Depends on the plugin's `pm-chat` skill (plugin roadmap).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A message gets a PM reply as a push within minutes, with history kept per project
- [ ] Rate limits of routines are respected and shown, never retried in a loop

2.title: Playwright e2e with axe
2.body:
Mobile and desktop projects, `BASE_URL`, local mock mode, stage via the Access service token.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `npx nx e2e console-e2e` runs against the Docker target and against stage
- [ ] Serious/critical axe violations fail the run

2.title: Web push end to end
2.body:
VAPID keys, subscription endpoint, `SwPush` client with the iOS "add to Home Screen" guide and permission only on a
tap, sending with pruning of dead subscriptions, badge count. Source: `docs/decisions/0001-stack-and-architecture.md` decision 8.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test push arrives on an installed iPhone PWA and on Mac
- [ ] Permission is never requested without a user gesture
